brief: Goldman Sachs desk note previewing the week of 14 September 2026. Setup: investor anxiety is high, net exposure in the 6th percentile and the largest macro ETF short selling since liberation day, while surface volatility stays calm at VIX 15, 27 sessions without a 100bps intraday band and a 130bps SPX one week straddle, a gap the desk attributes to 0dte flow in a tape where volumes are down almost 40 percent from July's record. Four catalysts follow. Oil: crude above 100 and Brent above 109, GS raised Brent and WTI forecasts on a new assumption that Middle East shipping is disrupted through 2027, so geopolitics raises global inflation risk as central banks tighten. Fed: GS now expects a Wednesday hike, read as a forced hike managing optics rather than fundamentals, which could calm nerves because one and done removes guesswork from the rest of 2026. Japan: 10y yields near 3 percent make domestic fixed income competitive, risking the loss of Japan as marginal buyer of global duration. Bonds: 10y near 5 percent and 30y above 5.3 percent constrain long duration high multiple equities. Desk trades: buy the AI hardware dip, short the consumer inertia basket.
